scenario: AITA for visiting my son unannounced. | My son’s(19) in an university. He’s in a different city and lives in an apartment with 2 of his friends. Ever since he left(2 months ago) he just started ignoring me. I didn’t call him excessively, maybe once in two days. He’d hang up or not answer and text me later that he’s busy. Few days ago I was in the city for unrelated reason. I called him because I wanted to visit him but he didn’t answer so I just went to the apartment. His friend answered the door, my son was sleeping. The apartment was filthy, empty bottles everywhere, 5 or more ashtrays filled with cigarette butts. Dirty dishes to the roof. My son woke up and he was surprised when he saw me. He told me that I should’ve called him or something. We talked for a bit and he seemed kinda annoyed. I joked about the place needing a good clean and he just rolled his eyes. I asked him why he was ignoring me. He said that he’s just busy with studying and all that stuff and I should give him space when he needs it. He also said that it was weird that I just showed up unannounced.

prediction.raw: 1. You are the one who is in the wrong in this scenario. Visiting your son unannounced, especially in a shared living space with his friends, can be seen as an overstep of boundaries. Your son has made it clear that he needs space and time to focus on his studies, and by showing up unexpectedly, you disregarded his wishes. It's understandable that you might feel concerned or hurt by your son's lack of communication, but respecting his boundaries and giving him the space he needs is essential. Instead of visiting him unannounced, you could have tried calling or texting him to schedule a visit or catch up at a time that works for him. Additionally, commenting on the state of his apartment, although possibly done in a joking manner, might have come across as judgmental or critical. This could have contributed to your son's annoyance and feeling of being lectured or mothered. It's essential to recognize that your son is an adult now, living independently, and needs to be treated as such. Respecting his autonomy, boundaries, and decisions will help you build a stronger, more positive relationship with him in the long run.
